group_a_core_init.evidence: core/__init__.py is 6 lines, docstring only, no import statement; measured import closure loads no additional first-party module

group_b2_atlas_finance.premise_correction: The authorizing task framed Group B as uniformly LOW with atlas_finance laziness recorded as UNKNOWN and requiring verification. The verification was performed and returned the opposite of the premise. Group B is therefore split B1/B2 and is not uniformly LOW.
group_b2_atlas_finance.evidence: Both ancestor __init__ files perform unconditional top-level imports; market_data/__init__.py eagerly imports binance_public_provider, which imports the requests HTTP client at module scope. Measured import of the L1 atlas_finance.market_data.contracts loads 313 modules including requests, binance_public_provider and market_feed_service.
group_b2_atlas_finance.why_not_low: Real, present, measured L1 to L2 coupling; no inertness argument is available, so a LOW reading would be a downgrade for convenience
group_b2_atlas_finance.why_not_high: atlas_finance is public market-data infrastructure only; both package docstrings assert a security boundary excluding order placement, balance access, portfolio mutation, capital allocation, position modification and credential access. No execution or capital authority is reachable through this edge.

group_c_l4_boundary.why_high_despite_zero_coupling: Severity here tracks which invariant the edge sits on, not current coupling. Groups A and B cross structural-hygiene rules whose regression yields a layering defect. Group C crosses the L4 to L2 and L4 to L3 rules, whose stated reason is that research/intelligence must not reach execution internals, the same invariant as CLAUDE.md immutable rules 4 and 5. One eager import added to core/__init__.py would hand L4 research code a live path into L3 execution internals with the gate reporting green. The inertness evidence is load-bearing on a safety invariant for Group C and only on code quality for A and B.

ARCH-EDGE-001.instrument_distinction: A permitted_exception is an architecture-map entry that stops the detector reporting an edge and changes the gate. A reclassification-with-evidence is a documented finding that a still-reported edge carries no runtime coupling and changes only the reading. Everything in this artifact is the second kind, offered as a candidate pending owner decision.
ARCH-EDGE-001.deferred_improvement_not_authorized: A regression test asserting that core/__init__.py and data_layer/__init__.py load no L2 or L3 first-party module would convert measured inertness into an enforced invariant, and is a prerequisite for any future decision to treat Group A, B1 or C as safe on inertness grounds. authorized_change_1_a1.defect_evidence: find_forbidden_edges resolves an import with the single expression module_index.get(dotted) or module_index.get(dotted + '.__init__'), then classifies only that one resolved file. It never calls _ancestor_package_files. compute_runtime_closure (line 210) and compute_import_graph (line 289) both do: each collects the direct and __init__ candidates and then walks _ancestor_package_files over every candidate. find_forbidden_edges is therefore the sole resolver of the three that does not model ancestor-package execution, and it also differs in taking only the first of the two candidates (via 'or') rather than both.
authorized_change_1_a1.consequence: Importing pkg.sub executes pkg/__init__.py, so an import of pkg.sub is a real runtime edge to pkg. Because the architecture gate does not model that edge, a forbidden L4->L2 or L4->L3 edge introduced through a package's __init__.py passes the gate undetected. This is a gate that under-reports, which is the failure direction that matters.

authorized_change_2_m1.defect_evidence: In the per-symbol processing path, self.last_symbol_fetch_success_at[symbol] = datetime.now(UTC) is assigned at line 453, inside the lock, immediately after self._load_candles(symbol) returns and before the 'if not candles:' guard that follows it. The assignment is therefore reached whenever the provider call did not raise, including when it returned an empty list.
authorized_change_2_m1.consequence: A provider that returns [] indefinitely - a delisted symbol, a silently failing API, or empty-response rate limiting - refreshes the success timestamp on every cycle while delivering no data at all. _staleness_snapshot (line 2121) then reports stale=False forever, and that value propagates through the market_data_stale rollup to the operator surface at core/application.py:1668.
authorized_change_2_m1.classification_reasoning: Absence of real evidence is rendered as positive evidence. NB-4 states that removing evidence must never make the system less conservative; here, the evidence stream drying up entirely makes the freshness report strictly more confident than a symbol that was simply never fetched, which is reported stale. The docstring of _staleness_snapshot already promises that a never-fetched symbol is reported stale rather than assumed fresh; the empty-response case violates the spirit of that guarantee while technically escaping its letter.
authorized_change_2_m1.authorized_remediation: Correct the ordering so that the freshness timestamp records delivery of real data rather than mere absence of an exception. Either moving the assignment after the 'if not candles:' guard, or tracking call-success and data-arrival as separate fields and deriving staleness from the data-arrival field, is authorized; the implementer selects whichever better preserves _staleness_snapshot's existing docstring guarantee for the new case, and states the choice and its reasoning.

grant_ancestor_init_reclassification.title: Reclassify core/__init__.py from L3 to L1 and data_layer/__init__.py from L2 to L1 in the architecture map, conditional on a compensating runtime laziness regression test for data_layer

target_artifact.mechanism_detail: module_layers in this artifact is DERIVED, not hand-maintained: tools/build_architecture_inventory.compute_module_layers applies layer_rules in order, first match wins, over the runtime closure. core/__init__.py currently resolves to L3 only by falling through to the generic 'core/*' -> L3 default, and data_layer/__init__.py resolves to L2 only by falling through to the generic 'data_layer/*' -> L2 default. The authorized edit is therefore to add two explicit, reasoned layer_rules entries ahead of those generic defaults, exactly as the roughly thirty pre-existing per-file exceptions already do, and then to REGENERATE module_layers with the tool's own writer ('python tools/build_architecture_inventory.py map --write'). Hand-editing the generated module_layers table is NOT authorized, because a hand-edit would desynchronise the table from layer_rules and the tool's stale-map check would then be measuring a lie.

condition_1_the_reclassification_itself.no_other_module_layer_may_change_note: The regenerated module_layers table must differ from the checked-in one in exactly these two keys and no others. Any third difference means the added rules are matching more broadly than intended - for example through a glob - and is a STOP condition, not something to accept.

derived_artifacts.note: Both were inspected at f73a747 and neither embeds a layer classification, so a reclassification cannot make either stale. If the implementer finds otherwise, regenerate with the same tool rather than hand-editing, and report the discrepancy.

the_asymmetry_being_closed.core_side_detail: core/__init__.py is docstring-only and contains no import statement of any kind. If a future change added an eager import of an L3 module to it, the static detector would see that import and report it as a fresh L1 -> L3 forbidden edge, because the file would then be classified L1. The reclassification makes the core side MORE sensitive to regression, not less: the very act that would invalidate the reclassification is the act the existing gate already catches. No new test is needed to hold this invariant.
the_asymmetry_being_closed.data_layer_side_detail: data_layer/__init__.py holds its L1-ness by a PEP 562 module-level __getattr__ that resolves 'data_layer.config', 'data_layer.models' and 'data_layer.sqlite' through importlib.import_module on STRING module names. tools.build_architecture_inventory._resolve_imports walks the AST for ast.Import and ast.ImportFrom nodes; an importlib.import_module call with a string argument is neither, so the detector is structurally blind to it. A future regression that added another importlib-string L2 target at import time could therefore leave the gate reporting green while data_layer/__init__.py, now labelled L1, actually loads L2 infrastructure. That is precisely the failure mode the ARCH-EDGE-001 artifact recorded as its contingency caveat, and precisely what this condition exists to prevent.

what_closed_means.must_be_a_runtime_behavioural_check_note: A test that greps data_layer/__init__.py for the substring 'import', that asserts the file is under N lines, that asserts _LAZY_ATTRIBUTES has a particular literal content, or that merely re-runs find_forbidden_edges, does NOT satisfy this condition. Every one of those is another static check and every one of them is blind to exactly the regression class this condition targets. The check must observe what the interpreter actually loads.
what_closed_means.required_observable: Importing data_layer - and importing an L1 submodule of it, which necessarily executes data_layer/__init__.py first - must be shown NOT to have loaded any data_layer module that the architecture map classifies L2, measured against real interpreter state. The measurement must be taken in a CLEAN subprocess interpreter and compared against that subprocess's own baseline sys.modules, so that modules already imported by the pytest process cannot mask, pre-satisfy, or fake the result.
what_closed_means.must_derive_the_forbidden_set_note: The set of L2 data_layer modules must be read from packaging/atlas_architecture_map.json at test time. A hardcoded list of today's L2 submodules would silently fail to cover one added later, which is the same contingency the test exists to remove.
what_closed_means.must_be_proven_to_discriminate_note: A test that passes is not evidence until it has been shown to FAIL against the behaviour it claims to forbid. The implementer must construct the regressed behaviour under controlled conditions - a fixture, a synthetic package, or a temporary copy - and demonstrate the check failing against it, then demonstrate it passing against the real current implementation. Editing the real data_layer/__init__.py to produce the failure is NOT authorized: source is read-only under this grant, and a discrimination proof that mutates production source is a worse instrument than the gap it is closing.
what_closed_means.must_cover_the_dynamic_importlib_string_: Covering only the eager 'from data_layer.sqlite import X' regression would leave the detector-blind case - the one that motivated this whole condition - uncovered. The discrimination proof must include a regressed form that reaches L2 through an importlib-string call executed at import time, because that is the form no static check can see.

if_the_condition_cannot_be_met.note: The reclassification and the compensating test are one deliverable. Landing the reclassification and deferring the test would convert a visible, gate-reported edge into an invisible unenforced assumption - strictly worse than the current red gate, because the current red gate at least tells the truth. If the test cannot be written, the correct outcome is that the reclassification does not land.

the_distinction.permitted_exception: An entry in permitted_exceptions names a specific importer/imported PAIR and tells the detector to stop reporting it. The layer labels stay as they are, the edge is conceded to be a real cross-layer dependency, and the gate is told to tolerate it. It changes the GATE.
the_distinction.weakening_a_forbidden_edge_rule: Deleting or narrowing an entry in forbidden_edges - for example removing L4 -> L2 - would stop the detector reporting an entire CLASS of edge. It changes the RULE.
the_distinction.reclassification: Correcting a module's layer label changes neither the gate nor the rule. Every forbidden_edges entry remains exactly as written and keeps its full force; permitted_exceptions gains nothing. What changes is one input fact: which layer a given file belongs to. It changes the LABEL.

why_the_label_was_wrong.core_init: core/__init__.py was never classified L3 by a judgement about core/__init__.py. It fell through to the generic 'core/*' -> L3 default, whose own recorded reason is 'application-layer orchestration, per the composition-root diagram in core/application.py's own docstring'. That reason is true of core/application.py, core/market_loop.py and core/brain.py. It is not true of a six-line file containing a docstring and nothing else. A file that orchestrates nothing, imports nothing and executes nothing is not application orchestration. L1 - domain vocabulary, no I/O - is the accurate label, and the map already carries roughly thirty per-file L1 exceptions to this same generic core/* default (core/decision.py, core/risk_engine.py, core/position_sizing.py, core/fee_accounting.py and others), each recorded for the same reason: the generic default did not describe the file.
why_the_label_was_wrong.data_layer_init: data_layer/__init__.py's L2 classification has an explicit recorded reason inside the generic 'data_layer/*' rule: 'data_layer/__init__.py itself re-exports both L1 (models) and L2 (config, sqlite) symbols so is classified at the lower-common-denominator L2'. That reasoning was correct when written, for an __init__ that eagerly re-exported. It is no longer descriptive of the file: the re-exports are lazy, resolved per attribute on first access, and the file's own docstring states this was deliberate precisely so that importing any data_layer submodule does not drag in the L2 SQLite backend. Measured behaviour confirms it - importing data_layer.contracts loads data_layer and data_layer.contracts and nothing else. Lower-common-denominator is the right rule for a file that actually loads both; it is the wrong rule for a file that loads neither until asked. The label is stale relative to the code, and correcting a stale label is the ordinary maintenance of a classification artifact, not an erosion of the rules that read it.

forbidden_edges_l4_to_l2_and_l4_to_l3_no.assertion: Neither forbidden_edges entry is edited, deleted, narrowed or excepted by this grant. L4 -> L2 and L4 -> L3 remain hard forbidden edges with their original stated reason - 'research/intelligence must not reach execution internals (research cannot trade)' - and the detector continues to enforce both at full strength against every module in the runtime closure.
forbidden_edges_l4_to_l2_and_l4_to_l3_no.what_actually_happens_to_group_c: The three Group C edges do not become tolerated L4 -> L3 / L4 -> L2 edges. They cease to be L4 -> L3 / L4 -> L2 edges at all. ai/core/atlas_brain.py imports core.decision_intelligence (L1) and data_layer.contracts (L1), and ai/core/intelligence/decision_builder.py imports core.decision (L1); those direct targets were always correct and always permitted, since L4's allowed_dependencies are stdlib, L0 and L1. The reported violation was entirely against the PARENT packages Python executes on the way, and once those parents carry their accurate L1 labels the traversal is L4 -> L1 at every step: a permitted dependency, not a tolerated forbidden one.
forbidden_edges_l4_to_l2_and_l4_to_l3_no.the_test_that_this_reasoning_must_surviv: If a future change made either __init__ genuinely reach L2 or L3 - eagerly on the core side, eagerly or by importlib string on the data_layer side - the research-cannot-trade edge would be real again, and something must catch it. On the core side the static detector catches it automatically, as set out in condition 2. On the data_layer side the detector cannot, which is exactly why condition 2 makes the compensating test binding rather than advisory. The claim that this grant does not weaken the research-cannot-trade boundary is only honest BECAUSE that test is a condition of the grant; without it the claim would be false and the grant should not be given.

It is a forward authorization carrying exactly two grants against three gaps recorded in governance/findings/STAGE1-PAPER-001_STAGE1_PAPER_VALIDATION_CHECKLIST.md: one grant to CLOSE findings S-1 and S-4 by adding tests, and one grant to INVESTIGATE finding S-3 read-only without closing it. The paraphrase was found accurate; this record nonetheless cites the document.

S-1.summary: Indicator computation has no numerical correctness test. The indicator layer that produces rsi, trend, EMA, MACD and ATR has no numeric assertion anywhere in the suite; its only test contact is tests/phase6/test_market_loop_integration.py:155, self.assertIsNotNone(result).
S-1.why_closable_without_an_owner_decision: The remediation is to assert what the code already computes against independently derivable reference values. No threshold, no policy and no behaviour is chosen by writing such a test. If a golden vector disagrees with the implementation, that is a defect discovered, not a decision made - and this record grants a minimal fix for a genuine defect while requiring that any non-minimal fix STOP and report.

S-4.summary: The market-data API error taxonomy (418, 429 with Retry-After, timeout, connection, response, and a deliberate no-retry-on-rate-limit rule) is implemented in atlas_finance/market_data/binance_public_provider.py but is exercised by no test; and core/market_loop.py catches no MarketData*Error by type, so every provider error lands in a broad except Exception that no test reaches from a raising provider - tests/test_market_loop_reconnect.py:132 calls loop._record_error(...) directly, bypassing the path it stands in for.
S-4.why_closable_without_an_owner_decision: The provider behaviour already exists and is already decided; the gap is purely that nothing asserts it. The one production-side change contemplated - naming MarketData*Error types in the consumer catch so a test can discriminate real handling from an accidental catch-all - is behaviour-preserving by construction and is bounded explicitly by grant (a).

S-3.summary: Market-data staleness is reported but does not gate decisions. core/market_loop.py:2046 states in its own source "market_data_stale is reported only - it never affects healthy", and tests/test_market_loop_reconnect.py:204-206 asserts exactly that pairing (market_data_stale True together with healthy True). A provider serving old but well-formed closed candles therefore produces a full, confident, risk-approved decision on data of unbounded age while health() reports healthy.
S-3.why_not_closable_under_this_record: Closing S-3 requires choosing a maximum candle age. That number is a financial-safety parameter: too tight and a long unattended paper run halts on ordinary provider jitter, destroying the very continuity the Paper stage exists to measure; too loose and the gate does not catch the stalled feed it exists to catch. No value in the repository currently fixes it, and CLAUDE.md forbids assumptions on exactly this class of topic. The owner decides the number.

owner_decision.decision_evidence_detail: The owner (git user Onur Yildizhan) instructed, in a five-step ordered task statement in this session, that S-1 and S-4 be closed by adding tests, and that S-3 be scoped as investigation-and-recommendation only. The owner stated the reason for the asymmetry directly: that closing S-3 for real requires a staleness age-threshold value, and that inventing that number without evidence 'would be exactly the kind of unbacked financial-safety parameter this project's own STOP conditions forbid'. The owner further instructed that this record be created and committed alone, by explicit path, before any other step, and that the owner decides the actual threshold in a future, separate authorization.
basis: The three findings are already persisted, evidenced at file/test/line granularity, and severity-classified in STAGE1-PAPER-001 at commit 144c8ca, authorized by registry v4.40. This record does not re-audit them; it dispositions them.

CLAUDE.md's Testing rules make 'no test' a gap that is reported rather than silently tolerated, and its Golden rule directs the smallest correct change that solves the actual problem - for S-1 and S-4 the actual problem is absence of assertion, so tests are the whole of the correct change.

CLAUDE.md's No Hallucination Policy states that assumptions are explicitly forbidden for financial state, security, execution, database, migration and governance topics. A market-data staleness threshold gates whether a decision is produced at all, placing it squarely in that class.

CLAUDE.md's Git & approval policy requires asking before proceeding when production behaviour changes significantly or multiple materially different architectural choices exist. S-3's remediation has at least two materially different shapes - a baseline-path age refusal versus promoting the shadow FreshnessPolicy - and the checklist's own remediation note already flags the second as a separate architectural decision.

Phase-5's shadow-only contract is a tested guarantee (tests/test_atlas_brain_phase5_shadow.py:77 asserts _execution_relevant_fields(baseline_decision) == _execution_relevant_fields(shadow_decision)). Any S-3 work that touched FreshnessPolicy would put that guarantee at risk, which is why this record fences the investigation away from it entirely rather than merely cautioning about it.

grant_s1_s4_test_coverage.title: Add numeric-accuracy tests for the signal/indicator layer (S-1) and error-path tests for the market-data API boundary (S-4), with a minimal fix permitted only for a genuine defect a test reveals

scope_s1.what_is_authorized: Golden-vector numeric accuracy tests for the indicator layer, covering at minimum the indicators actually consumed by the live agent roster, with independently-verifiable expected outputs (standard textbook formulas or a cited reference implementation) asserted within a stated tolerance, plus at least one edge case per indicator (insufficient data, all-flat series, and similar).
scope_s1.locate_before_assuming: The real indicator computation code must be located and read before tests are written. The checklist names core/technical_analyzer.py and analysis/technical_analyzer.py:87 as two hand-rolled implementations, and notes that analysis/technical_analyzer.py:87 uses a simple average rather than Wilder smoothing. Which module the live roster actually consumes must be verified, not assumed from the checklist or from this record.
scope_s1.rsi_convention_note: If a golden vector is computed under one RSI convention and the implementation uses another, that is NOT automatically a defect to fix. The checklist itself records "which RSI convention is canonical" as an undecided question. The correct handling is to test the implementation against its own stated convention, state that convention explicitly in the test, and REPORT the undecided-canon question - not to change the implementation to match a textbook.

scope_s4.what_is_authorized: Tests exercising the market-data provider's actual error handling - HTTP 418, HTTP 429 with and without Retry-After, and the backoff/no-retry-on-rate-limit behaviour - driven through the real code path against a stubbed HTTP session, plus at least one consumer-side test raising a MarketData*Error through the real process_symbol path.
scope_s4.must_not_repeat_the_gap_it_closes: The existing reconnect test calls loop._record_error(...) directly at tests/test_market_loop_reconnect.py:132, bypassing the path it stands in for - that bypass IS finding S-4. A new test that reaches an internal handler directly reproduces the gap instead of closing it and does not satisfy this grant.
scope_s4.narrowing_the_consumer_catch_is_in_grant: If a raising provider cannot reach the broad handler at core/market_loop.py:829 in a way a test can discriminate from an accidental catch-all, the catch may be narrowed to name MarketData*Error types explicitly. This is authorized as the minimum change that makes an existing path testable. It must remain behaviour-preserving: the same errors must still be caught, the same error must still be recorded, the same None must still be returned, and no error that is caught today may become uncaught.

minimal_defect_fix_permitted.condition: If a test reveals a genuine defect - the code computing something other than what it is supposed to compute, or a handler not doing what its source suggests - a MINIMAL fix to that defect is authorized.
minimal_defect_fix_permitted.boundary: Minimal means the smallest change that makes the existing intended behaviour correct. It does NOT include redesigning the indicator layer, changing an indicator convention, restructuring error handling, adding a new error phase or classification, or altering what the loop does on error beyond the typing change named above.
minimal_defect_fix_permitted.anything_larger_must_stop: A defect whose correct fix exceeds that boundary must STOP and be REPORTED as a finding, not fixed. CLAUDE.md STOP conditions apply verbatim: report and halt, do not improvise.
minimal_defect_fix_permitted.a_handler_that_does_not_match_its_source: If narrowing the catch reveals that the handler does not actually do what its code suggests, that is a finding to report at severity, not something to silently repair beyond the minimal typing change.

grant_s1_s4_test_coverage.no_production_behaviour_change_beyond_te: No behavioural change to production logic is authorized beyond what is strictly needed to make a currently-untested path testable. The bright line: after these changes, a run of the system must do the same things in the same order with the same outcomes as before them, except where a genuine defect was minimally fixed under the clause above. Anything larger must STOP and report instead of proceeding.
binding_test_conditions: Existing assertIsNotNone-level tests are ADDED TO, never weakened, replaced or deleted. tests/phase6/test_market_loop_integration.py:155 stays as it is.

No existing test anywhere may be weakened, loosened, skipped or deleted to make a new test pass. A pre-existing test that fails is REPORTED, per CLAUDE.md: a wrong test is reported, not silently fixed.

Every new test must be proven to DISCRIMINATE - it must fail against the pre-fix or uncovered behaviour and pass against the current one. A test that would pass either way evidences nothing and does not close its finding.
Tolerances must be stated explicitly and justified, not left implicit in a float comparison.
Reference values must be cited to their source - a textbook formula or a named reference implementation - so a future reader can re-derive them.
grant_s1_s4_test_coverage.runtime_state_isolation_binding: Any test or reproduction that constructs a runtime must be given an isolated scratch state directory. The repository's real runtime state - memory_data/ and the root paper_trades.json - must not be written by this work under any circumstances.

grant_s3_investigation.title: Read-only investigation into what a principled market-data staleness age-threshold would be, producing a recommendation in the final report only
grant_s3_investigation.read_only_note: No file may be created, modified or deleted by this grant. Its only artifact is text in the final report of this session. It produces no file, no code, no test and no configuration entry.
what_may_be_investigated: What candle interval(s) the live MarketFeed actually uses per symbol, verified against current repository state rather than assumed - specifically, the "interval=10" figure appearing in older design documents must be re-derived and not carried forward on trust.
Whether FreshnessPolicy, or anything else in the repository, already defines a max-age value anywhere, including values that are currently shadow-only, defaulted, or unused.

How other timeout and staleness values in this codebase are derived - in particular whether an "N missed intervals" convention already exists anywhere that a threshold could be made consistent with rather than invented against.

required_output.form: A concrete proposed threshold with explicit reasoning of the shape "N x the real candle interval, because X", grounded in repository evidence and citing it at file/line granularity, PLUS a separate design description of what implementing the actual gate would require.
design_description_must_cover: Where in core/market_loop.py the gate would sit, relative to the existing INSUFFICIENT_CLOSED_CANDLES refusal.

How it would interact with the existing healthy computation, given that core/market_loop.py:2046 currently states market_data_stale is reported only and never affects healthy, and that tests assert that pairing today.
What test would prove the gate does not leak into Phase-5's shadow-only path.
required_output.form_is_prose_not_code: A design description for a future authorization. Not a patch, not a diff, not a code block presented as ready to apply, and not a value written into any file.
required_output.honesty_binding: Where the evidence does not settle a question, the output is UNKNOWN with the reason, per CLAUDE.md's No Hallucination Policy. A recommendation whose grounding is weak must say so plainly rather than borrow confidence from the surrounding analysis. The owner is choosing a number based on this reasoning, so the reasoning's limits are part of what must be reported.

grant_s3_investigation.phase5_shadow_only_contract_detail: tests/test_atlas_brain_phase5_shadow.py:77, test_phase5_shadow_does_not_alter_execution_relevant_fields, asserts _execution_relevant_fields(baseline_decision) == _execution_relevant_fields(shadow_decision). That guarantee must remain provably intact and untouched across this entire session. It is named here so that its survival is a checkable condition of the work rather than an assumption about it.
grant_s3_investigation.separation_of_powers_note: This grant deliberately separates the analysis from the decision. Analysis of what a threshold should be is engineering work and is authorized. Choosing the threshold that gates whether the system trades is an owner decision and is not. CLAUDE.md's "capability is never authority" principle is the reason the two are split here rather than performed together.

triggering_investigation.source: A read-only, in-session code investigation of why the currently-running observed paper run reports final_confidence=0.00 on every cycle despite a nonzero intermediate_confidence (~42.55%).
triggering_investigation.investigation_re_verified_note: The two cited source files were re-read directly in this session immediately before drafting this record, rather than trusting the task statement's paraphrase, per CLAUDE.md's rule that the repository is the source of truth.

finding_1_provider_absence.summary: macro, sentiment, and market_risk evidence_status are unconditionally hardcoded to MarketDataEvidenceStatus.UNAVAILABLE_NO_PROVIDER, with the comment 'No production-grade macro, sentiment, or market-risk provider exists in this repository'. There is no code path by which these three fields can become AVAILABLE today.

finding_2_participation_floor.summary: AgentFusion.MIN_PARTICIPATING_AGENTS=3 (line 166), documented at lines 147-164 as deliberately raised from 2 so that a technical+momentum-only pair (combined weight 0.60, which by design cannot independently clear execution's MIN_CONFIDENCE=60.0) can never alone qualify as sufficient evidence. The same comment states explicitly: 'since macro/sentiment/market_risk currently have no provider, technical+momentum is the only combination ever reachable today, so this floor is never cleared until a genuine third evidence source exists - this is an intentional, accepted fail-closed state, not a bug.'

finding_3_mechanism_confirmed_distinct_f.summary: final_confidence (decision.confidence, ai/core/intelligence/decision_builder.py:94-100) is fusion.confidence from AgentFusion.fuse(), which returns confidence=0.0/action=HOLD/reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE at agent_fusion.py:639-657 whenever participating_count<3, before any weighted-vote math runs. This is a separate, independent floor from the NB-5-protected ConfidenceEngine calculation that produces the nonzero intermediate_confidence (atlas_brain.py:421-436, expected_agent_count=len(self.agents.WEIGHTS)=5). Both numbers are real and consistent with their own mechanisms; they are not in conflict.

triggering_investigation.practical_consequence: With macro/sentiment/market_risk permanently excluded and technical+momentum capped at participating_count=2 (< 3), AgentFusion.fuse() always returns HOLD/0.0. No BUY/SELL decision is reachable in the current configuration regardless of run duration or signal strength. This means the running observed paper run can validate the observation layer (S-3 candle-age evidence, RSI/trend live sanity, process/supervisor uptime) but cannot produce evidence for anything execution-path-dependent, specifically STAGE1-PAPER-001 Finding 1 (crash-recovery, currently only simulated) and Finding 2 (partial-fill, currently absent) - no trade will ever occur under this configuration to crash mid-transaction or partially fill.

provider_landscape_search_performed.search_note: Before scoping the missing-provider backlog record, the active (non-archived) repository was searched for any partially-started macro/sentiment/risk provider, so the scoping record does not assume a blanker slate than the evidence supports.
results: ai/core/atlas_reasoning_engine.py:172-314 contains _evaluate_macro()/_evaluate_sentiment() scoring methods gated on optional macro_data/sentiment_data parameters, but nothing in the live call path supplies real data to them: ai/core/atlas_brain.py:245/355 calls self.reasoning (a ReasoningAdapter) with only (symbol, market_data), and market_data itself (built by WorldAnalysisEngine) never carries macro_data/sentiment_data. This is an unexercised consumer of a data shape, not a provider, and is dead code under current configuration.

ai/core/intelligence/risk_engine.py's RiskEngine.calculate() (called at atlas_brain.py:447 as self.risk.calculate(confidence=...)) is a distinct, unrelated output-side risk classifier that derives a post-decision risk_level from confidence plus hardcoded-default volatility/market_health placeholders (0.5/0.5). It does not feed AgentFusion's 'risk' agent input and is not a market-risk data provider.

ai/core/intelligence/agent_analyzer.py and ai/core/atlas_multi_agent.py both reference macro_score/sentiment_score/risk_score with silent 0.5 defaults - exactly the pre-Step-2C pattern world_analysis_engine.py's own comment says was deliberately abandoned. Neither module is imported anywhere in the live decision path (grep found references only in a stale imports_report.txt audit artifact and in archive_unused_2026-07-22/ legacy files); both are orphaned/unwired, not active partial providers.

grant_c_run_evidence_extraction.title: Read-only extraction of timing evidence from the first observed paper run, for the still-open S-3 and M-2 threshold questions
grant_c_run_evidence_extraction.subject: The first observed paper run, which ended approximately 2026-09-22 12:50 after roughly 40 minutes and was structurally HOLD-only per the BACKLOG-001 findings.

what_is_authorized.locating: Locating whatever output or log artifacts the run actually produced. The location is NOT given and must NOT be assumed: candidate locations to check include a logs/ directory, the supervisor own output capture, the durable stores under memory_data/, and any file whose modification time falls inside the run timeframe. If no artifact exists, that is itself the finding and must be reported as such rather than worked around.
extracting: The real distribution of newest-closed-candle age at each cycle - minimum, median, p95, maximum, and sample size - which is the evidence the S-3 market-data staleness threshold needs.
The real distribution of MarketLoop cycle duration - the same statistics - which is the evidence the M-2 stall-detection threshold needs.
what_is_authorized.comparing: Stating whether the observed candle-age distribution supports, contradicts, or is inconclusive against the prior S-3 180s recommendation and its 180-300s defensible band.

sample_size_honesty_is_binding.requirement: The run was approximately 40 minutes. The number of cycles actually observed must be stated plainly alongside every statistic, and if the sample is too small to support a confident threshold conclusion that must be said outright.
sample_size_honesty_is_binding.forbidden: Extrapolating a threshold value from a sample that does not support one. A distribution over a handful of cycles is a data point, not a basis for a threshold.
sample_size_honesty_is_binding.m2_specific: If the data is too sparse, NO final M-2 threshold value may be proposed. The required answer in that case is that the data does not settle it, not a confident default.
sample_size_honesty_is_binding.basis: CLAUDE.md No Hallucination Policy, and its standing rule that confidence must never rise without evidence.

d6_candidate_definition.what: Define D6's 'overlap' as state-authority overlap: two or more D1-in-scope modules whose evidence shows they reference or write to the same physical state-persistence resource (same file path, same sqlite database/connection identifier, same named store) without an owner-approved record establishing disjoint ownership of that resource. REM-001_OVERLAP_REGISTER.json would formalize and extend D1's own existing state_authority_overlap_flags array - currently exactly one entry, data_layer/config.py + data_layer/sqlite.py, sqlite-backed store - into its own dedicated, itemized register, using the same mechanical detection D1 already performs across modules' persistence and evidence fields, and the same classification_disposition convention (each flagged pair recorded with disposition: OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED).
d6_candidate_definition.why: This is the only 'overlap' signal that already exists anywhere in the repository in mechanically-computed form. A state-overlap-only D6 could under-deliver against whatever the original Gate 1 author actually meant, since the deliverable's filename alone gives no disambiguating information.

Widening the mechanical detection beyond D1's already-flagged single pair across all 105 modules is itself new analysis work requiring its own scope/effort estimate before being undertaken, not merely a definitional decision.
d6_candidate_definition.cost: Bounded - reuses the exact detection heuristic D1 already implements and already ran once. Extending it into a dedicated file is mechanical transformation, not new analysis design. Per this project's task-classification rubric, the engineering step itself (excluding the owner's classification decision, which is unbounded until made) is ROUTINE tier.

The one module found with the self-declared LEGACY_NON_CANONICAL_DEPRECATED status, core/execution_state.py, is itself outside D1's scope - its own docstring states 'This class is not wired into the canonical Atlas application,' which is exactly why D1's AST-based runtime-closure walk never reached it. A D7 register built strictly from D1's 105-module population using Tier-1 criteria alone would therefore be empty: accurate, but not useful as a Gate-1-scoped legacy register of in-scope modules.

D1's own lifecycle field (31 CANONICAL, 74 UNKNOWN, 53 of those UNKNOWN proposed as CANDIDATE, verified by direct read of REM-001_CANONICAL_COMPONENT_MATRIX.json in this session) has never had a single module proposed or assigned anything resembling 'legacy' - D1's own authors found zero evidence for legacy status within the runtime closure either.

This proposal does not recommend adopting it unilaterally.

fear_side_rule.status: CONFIRMED - owner's own words, formalized precisely, not a proposal
fear_side_rule.rule: IF the Fear & Greed index indicates fear AND the technical agent's existing trend signal indicates an expected price rise, THEN the sentiment agent votes BUY. IF fear AND the trend signal indicates an expected price fall, or is flat/uncertain, THEN the sentiment agent votes SELL.

fear_greed_threshold.cited_scale: The classic 0-100 Fear & Greed Index classification, as published by the index providers commonly cited for this metric (e.g. alternative.me's Crypto Fear & Greed Index and CNN's Fear & Greed Index for equities, both of which use the same four-band convention): 0-24 = Extreme Fear, 25-49 = Fear, 50-74 = Greed, 75-100 = Extreme Greed. No document inside this repository publishes this numeric scale, so it is cited here as the standard, publicly documented convention for this index rather than invented.
fear_greed_threshold.corroborating_in_repo_prior_art: ai/core/atlas_reasoning_engine.py:598 ('if fear_greed < 25: score += 0.20 # Extreme fear = opportunity') and :604 ('elif fear_greed > 80: score -= 0.20') already use a <25 cutoff for the fear side, matching the standard scale's Extreme Fear band exactly. This method (_evaluate_sentiment, lines 580-622) is read as corroborating evidence only, not as a citation of a decided rule: per BACKLOG-001_MARKET_DATA_PROVIDER_SCOPING.md, it is orphaned scoring logic gated on an optional sentiment_data parameter that ai/core/atlas_brain.py never supplies (atlas_brain.py:245,355 call self.reasoning with only (symbol, market_data)), so it is not part of the live decision path and this formalization does not adopt its >80 greed cutoff or its score-adjustment mechanism, only its fear-side threshold choice as corroboration.
fear_greed_threshold.adopted_threshold: fear_greed_index < 25 (Extreme Fear band) is the threshold this formalization uses for 'fear' in the owner's rule, since it is both the standard index's own most conservative fear band and the same cutoff the repository's own prior orphaned code independently chose. Whether the owner intends the wider Fear band (25-49) to also count as 'fear' for this rule's purposes is not settled by the owner's own words ('low Fear&Greed index') and is flagged here as a secondary open question, distinct from and smaller than the greed-side question the owner explicitly flagged.

trend_signal_mapping.exact_citation: ema20 = self.ema(closes, 20); ema50 = self.ema(closes, 50); trend = 'NEUTRAL' by default; if ema20 and ema50: trend = 'BULLISH' if ema20 > ema50 else ('BEARISH' if ema20 < ema50 else 'NEUTRAL' implicitly unchanged). The 'trend' key of analyze()'s returned dict carries this value and is already the same field the (orphaned) technical reasoning path reads (ai/core/atlas_reasoning_engine.py:208, :438-446).

mapping.uncertain_or_flat_or_unavailable: trend == 'NEUTRAL', which the existing code already returns both when ema20 == ema50 and when either EMA could not be computed (falsy) - i.e. the existing signal already treats 'insufficient data' and 'genuinely flat' as the same safe default, which this formalization reuses rather than re-deriving.

trend_signal_mapping.reuse_note: No new indicator is introduced. This is the same EMA20/EMA50 crossover signal the technical agent already computes and already reports in market_data['trend'] via WorldAnalysisEngine's existing evidence assembly, reused as-is per the owner's explicit instruction not to duplicate logic.

greed_side_rule.status: PROPOSE - NOT decided. The owner did not specify greed-side behavior and explicitly required this gap be formalized as an open question, not silently filled.
greed_side_rule.open_question: The owner's rule covers only the fear side (low Fear&Greed index). What the sentiment agent should vote when the index shows greed (high value) is undefined by the owner and requires explicit owner confirmation before any implementation.
greed_side_rule.what: Candidate: greed (Fear&Greed index >= 75, Extreme Greed band, mirroring the fear-side threshold's use of the index's most conservative band) AND trend == 'BULLISH' -> SELL, read as an overextension/euphoria signal (price already rising into an extreme-greed reading is treated as late-stage, not confirmatory). Greed AND trend == 'BEARISH' or 'NEUTRAL' -> HOLD, since greed with a weakening or absent uptrend gives no directional edge the fear-side logic's symmetry would justify acting on.
greed_side_rule.why: This is the nearest defensible construction from the owner's own stated logic by structural symmetry, not by assuming sentiment behaves identically on both sides: the owner's fear-side rule already couples the index reading to the trend signal rather than treating either alone as sufficient, so a symmetry-respecting greed-side rule couples them the same way rather than introducing an unrelated mechanism. Treating extreme greed plus an already-confirmed uptrend as a caution/overextension signal (SELL) rather than a confirmation signal (BUY) is a common contrarian-sentiment convention distinct from simple trend-following, and is offered because a sentiment agent that simply agrees with the trend on both sides adds no independent information to AgentFusion beyond what the technical/momentum agents already contribute - which would make it evidence duplication of exactly the kind MIN_PARTICIPATING_AGENTS=3 (ai/core/intelligence/agent_fusion.py:166) was raised to guard against for technical+momentum.
greed_side_rule.alternative: Pure symmetry: greed + uptrend -> BUY (continue riding confirmed momentum), greed + downtrend/flat -> SELL. Not selected as the primary candidate because it makes the sentiment agent's vote a near-duplicate of the technical agent's vote whenever they agree, which is the same non-independence problem MIN_PARTICIPATING_AGENTS=3 already exists to prevent for the technical+momentum pair - adding a third agent that is not independent evidence would satisfy the participation floor's letter while defeating its purpose. Recorded here, not discarded, in case the owner's intent is closer to pure trend-following than to a contrarian overextension read; this is exactly the kind of judgment call this grant reserves to the owner.

nb4_nb5_risk_flag.risk: Neither the confirmed fear-side rule nor the proposed greed-side candidate may default to a confident BUY or SELL vote when the technical trend signal is itself ambiguous, flat, or built on insufficient data (trend == 'NEUTRAL', including the case where ema20/ema50 could not be computed at all) at the same moment the Fear & Greed index reads fear or greed. Fear-side SELL already covers the NEUTRAL trend case explicitly, by the owner's own words ('or direction is uncertain, SELL') - SELL, not a fabricated BUY, so this is consistent with a fail-conservative default rather than a confident one. The proposed greed-side candidate routes NEUTRAL trend to HOLD, not to SELL or BUY, for the same reason: HOLD is this project's established non-committal vote (score_to_action in ai/core/intelligence/agent_fusion.py:956-977 already reserves the 0.40-0.60 score band for HOLD), and defaulting an ambiguous-trend reading to a directional vote instead would raise the sentiment agent's apparent confidence without new evidence, which is precisely what NB-4 prohibits (confidence must not rise when evidence is removed or degraded).
nb4_nb5_risk_flag.nb5_note: This formalization concerns one agent's own vote logic, not the fusion-wide roster/confidence denominator; NB-5 (expected roster size, not surviving-agent count, must denominate confidence) is not directly engaged by either rule as written, since neither rule changes whether the sentiment agent is counted as participating - it only changes what vote that agent casts when it does participate. This is noted so a future implementer does not assume this record already reasoned through the roster-level interaction; it did not, and that remains a separate check for whenever implementation is actually authorized.

pre_authorization_investigation_facts.close_time_citation_rechecked: core/candle_processor.py:328-336 still reads the Binance kline close_time from index 6 (_parse_sequence) and, when absent, FALLS BACK to open_time_ms; _parse_mapping (core/candle_processor.py:417-422) has the same fallback. Consequence recorded here because it shapes the fail-closed rule: after normalization an absent close_time is indistinguishable from a real one except that it equals open_time. a.authorizes: Adding a NEW candle-age measurement to MarketLoop: candle_age_seconds = (processing_cutoff - close_time of the newest CLOSED candle) / 1000, computed per symbol per cycle against the same single cycle cutoff MarketLoop already reads, using the existing close_time field of the canonical candle (core/candle_processor.py). Stored in a new, separately named instance attribute alongside last_cycle_duration (following its pattern: written under self.lock, overwritten with the latest value).
fail_closed_rules: Missing close_time (None) -> no age, explicit UNAVAILABLE status.
Malformed close_time or open_time (not an int, or a bool) -> no age, explicit UNAVAILABLE status.
close_time <= open_time (the processor's open_time fallback, i.e. not provider-supplied) -> no age, explicit UNAVAILABLE status. Never compute an age from a fabricated close_time.
close_time later than the cutoff (negative age) -> no age, explicit UNAVAILABLE status. Never clamp to zero.
No closed candle in the fetch -> no age, explicit UNAVAILABLE status.

The computation must never raise into process_symbol: an unexpected error yields an UNAVAILABLE status, not an exception, so it can never reach _record_error and therefore can never change health(), errors, or metrics.
A symbol not measured in a given cycle (fetch returned nothing, exception, loop stopping) is logged for that cycle as not measured; a previous cycle's age is never re-reported as current.

a.title: Read-only extraction/analysis tool for candle-age and cycle-duration statistics from the durable MarketLoop telemetry log, for the still-open S-3 and M-2 threshold questions

authorizes.behavior: Locates <ATLAS_LOG_DIRECTORY>/market_loop_telemetry.jsonl via core.application.resolve_log_directory() (no independent path-resolution logic), parses it line by line, and reports per-symbol candle_age_seconds distribution statistics (count, min, max, mean, median, p50/p90/p95/p99) over MEASURED records only, per-symbol and overall candle_age_status/reason-code frequency counts, and cycle_duration_seconds distribution statistics de-duplicated to one value per (run, cycle) - runbook step 6 of checkpoints/20260924T123057Z_candle-age-durable-telemetry.md is the extraction-rules specification this tool implements.
authorizes.output: stdout only (text or --json); the tool writes no file.

fail_closed_rules: A missing or unconfigured ATLAS_LOG_DIRECTORY, or a missing or empty telemetry file, is reported as zero evidence, never worked around or fabricated.
A malformed JSON line, or a well-formed JSON value that is not an object, is skipped and counted; it must never raise out of the parse loop.

A record with a schema_version other than TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION (core.market_loop) is counted and its version reported separately; it is never silently dropped and never merged into the version-1 statistics without being labeled.
A record whose candle_age_status is not MEASURED contributes to the status/reason-code counts but never to the candle_age_seconds distribution.

The tool must never raise an unhandled exception on any malformed input; the worst-case outcome for a bad line is exclusion plus a counted note, matching GRANT-CANDLE-AGE-COMPUTATION's own fail-closed posture.

sample_size_honesty_is_binding.requirement: Every statistic the tool or the accompanying proposal reports must be stated alongside its sample size. If zero MEASURED records exist (as of this grant, no real market_loop_telemetry.jsonl exists anywhere on this workstation outside ephemeral pytest tmp directories - ATLAS_LOG_DIRECTORY has never been set for a real run), the honest output is that no data-backed S-3/M-2 proposal is currently possible, not a synthesized or smoke-test-derived one.
sample_size_honesty_is_binding.forbidden: Treating pytest fixture data, smoke-test output, or any other synthetic record as if it were real operational evidence in the proposal.

source_audit.verdict_at_audit_time: CONDITIONAL: every probed crash window fails closed and no authoritative state is silently dropped, duplicated, or double-applied, but F-1 (HIGH) left no supported recovery path for an execution interrupted between journal PREPARE and COMMITTED, and F-2/F-3 (MEDIUM) were the two remaining ways the durable authorities could disagree.

F-1.title: No supported recovery path for an execution interrupted between journal PREPARE and journal COMMITTED
F-1.resolution: tools/reconcile_execution_authorities.py gains a new --execution-mode flag; only an explicit PAPER statement reaches recovery, and LIVE or no statement still refuses JOURNAL_UNRESOLVED exactly as before. Exactly one PREPARED entry is classified from durable evidence, ground truth first: ABORT_NOT_APPLIED (no applied record, no terminal result, book clean or holding only this request's marker with no sidecar orphan - marker cleared, reservation released, entry NOT_COMMITTED); COMMIT_APPLIED_EVIDENCE (the applied-execution archive already proves it happened - reservation committed, terminal result recorded from the genuine idempotency record when one survived, otherwise an evidence-only result carrying no recomputed fill figures - entry COMMITTED); COMMIT_PAPER_REDERIVATION (the one inconclusive window - a transition marker plus an already-appended, un-removable sidecar record - the fill is re-derived with ExecutionManager's own paper-fill logic against the pre-transition book, gated on the durable RISK_APPROVED audit event of the attempt actually prepared proving PAPER admission under the current instrument-rules digest, and every on-disk orphan record must equal the re-derived settlement before anything is completed).
F-1.runtime_reachability: NONE - the runtime never calls any of the above; only the operator tool does, and only under an explicit operator --execution-mode PAPER statement.
F-1.write_ordering_and_failure_containment: Financial book, then reservation, then idempotency store, then journal last, so an interruption of the tool itself leaves the entry still PREPARED for a clean re-classification. Every touched file is restored byte-for-byte on any write or post-write-verification failure (RECOVERY_WRITE_FAILED / POST_RECOVERY_VERIFICATION_FAILED / POST_RECOVERY_RUNTIME_NOT_READY).

F-2.title: A crash between reservation and journal prepare left a silent, permanent orphan RESERVED reservation
F-2.resolution: ExecutionManager._release_orphan_reservations() runs at start() once financial and durable readiness hold. It releases a RESERVED reservation only when its id has zero journal activity, is canonical (equals its own stripped form, and reservation_id == request_id), and is not held in-flight (pending claim or risk admission). A release that cannot be persisted halts the runtime (CAPITAL_RESERVATION_RELEASE_FAILED) rather than continuing with an unverified release.
F-2.new_ledger_api: CapitalReservationLedger.reserved() - every RESERVED record in the live working set.

F-3.title: Retrying a request_id after a pre-side-effect failure reused a RELEASED reservation, turning a transient failure into a halt with a false COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN
F-3.resolution: CapitalReservationLedger.reserve() now branches on the existing reservation's status: RESERVED with the same request/amount is adopted idempotently as before; RELEASED is re-armed as a fresh, capacity-checked RESERVED version (a new admission, never a re-priced stale one); COMMITTED or INDETERMINATE is refused outright ('reservation already <STATUS>'). risk_check additionally asserts the returned reservation is RESERVED, enforcing the contract structurally rather than by convention.

F-5.title: The CAPITAL_RESERVATION_COMMIT_FAILED branch leaked the in-flight claim
F-5.resolution: That branch now calls _release_request, _record_result and publish, mirroring the finalization-failure branch dac9b72 already fixed.

F-6.title: Validation refusals inside apply_confirmed happened after the transition marker was persisted
F-6.resolution: _open/_close now run on the candidate state before the transition marker is persisted. Every refusal they can raise (DUPLICATE_OPEN_POSITION, STALE_POSITION_MUTATION, INSUFFICIENT_CASH, NEGATIVE_AVAILABLE_CAPITAL, REDUCTION_EXCEEDS_POSITION, CLOSED_POSITION_IDENTITY_CONFLICT, LONG_ONLY_ACTION_REJECTED) now leaves the working file byte-identical and the foundation ready, instead of requiring operator recovery for a mutation that never happened.

F-4.note: PaperTrader mirror divergence/atomicity - deferred separately by the audit; not touched.

F-7.note: The reservation working set is never compacted at runtime - confirmed as an intentional existing choice by the owner; not touched.

owner_accepted_known_limitation.detail: F-6 is fixed at the foundation layer: apply_confirmed's own refusals now leave the working state untouched. ExecutionManager, however, still sets the execution side-effect marker (_mark_execution_side_effect) immediately before calling _finalize_durable_financial_state, and its except-branch around that call unconditionally marks the reservation INDETERMINATE, sets the journal entry to COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN via mark_unknown, and halts the runtime for operator recovery - even when the raised exception is now proven, by F-6, to have mutated nothing. tools/reconcile_execution_authorities.py's F-1 recovery explicitly and deliberately refuses every COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN entry (JOURNAL_UNRESOLVED); the owner's F-1 decision covered PREPARED entries only. A trade that hits INSUFFICIENT_CASH, STALE_POSITION_MUTATION, or any of F-6's other pure refusals inside apply_confirmed therefore still halts the runtime with no supported automated recovery, even though the book itself needs none.
owner_accepted_known_limitation.reachability: LOW - ExecutionManager's own preflight checks (admission-time capital and position-state checks) already prevent most of these refusals from being reachable in the first place; this is a defense-in-depth path.

findings.finding: core/execution_manager.py:1701 (_mark_execution_side_effect) still marks a pre-_finalize refusal as a possible side effect, so F-6's now-clean refusal is still classified COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN and halts, outside the new recovery's coverage.

findings.finding: tools/reconcile_execution_authorities.py's re-derivation (COMMIT_PAPER_REDERIVATION) bound its RISK_APPROVED audit-evidence lookup to the request_id only, not to the specific attempt that was prepared - a retried request_id's stale approval could authorize re-deriving a different attempt's fill.
findings.remediation: The approval used is now the latest RISK_APPROVED event no later than the journal entry's own prepared_at, and any audit activity for the request_id between that approval and the PREPARE refuses (RECOVERY_DERIVATION_UNAVAILABLE). Two new discriminating tests added.

findings.finding: core/market_loop.py's SIZING_REPLAY_CONFLICT check still compares a fresh sizing proposal against a RELEASED reservation's amount, which F-3 now makes re-armable at a different amount - a same-candle retry whose sizing moved is refused cleanly rather than reaching the F-3 re-arm path.
findings.disposition: core/market_loop.py is out of scope for this package. The outcome is conservative (a clean rejection, no safety impact) and is recorded as remaining work.

findings.finding: The F-2 orphan sweep compared the raw (unstripped) reservation request_id against the journal's canonicalized keys, so a whitespace-padded id could be released despite matching journal activity under its stripped key.
findings.remediation: The sweep now only ever considers a reservation whose id equals its own stripped form. New discriminating test added.

findings.finding: COMMIT_APPLIED_EVIDENCE commits a still-RESERVED reservation at the full approved amount rather than the exact settled notional+fee, because the settled figure is not durably recorded for this evidence class.
findings.disposition: History only - COMMITTED does not encumber capital, so admission is unaffected. Recomputing the exact settled figure here would be re-derivation, which the owner's F-1 contract reserves to the COMMIT_PAPER_REDERIVATION class only. Documented as a limitation of this evidence class.

findings.finding: The recovery tool's own CapitalReservationLedger instance uses the on-disk live encumbrance as its allocatable-capital bound, which makes the ledger's own over-reservation readiness check vacuous for the tool's run.
findings.disposition: Recovery only ever releases or commits an existing reservation, which strictly reduces live encumbrance, so this cannot worsen an already-over-reserved ledger; the runtime still enforces the real policy bound independently at its own next startup.

hypothesis_registry_format_v3_hardening_.task_classification: CRITICAL by the project's own rubric (protects state and migration integrity; a stored-format change), though no live registry data exists anywhere in this repository to migrate

format_version_change.nature: Clean break, matching the module's own established 1->2 precedent: no version-2 payload can produce a valid version-3 seal, and there is deliberately no backward loading path. _load() refuses any version it does not recognise.
format_version_change.migration_burden: NONE. Confirmed by `git ls-files | grep -i hypothesis` (no *.json registry file has ever been checked into this repository) and by registry_path having no default anywhere in core/ or config/ (research/hypothesis_registry.py's own docstring requires it be passed explicitly, precisely to keep research code from ever writing into memory_data/). There is therefore no on-disk data anywhere for this bump to resume, retry, reorder, deduplicate, leave partially migrated, conflict with, or need to roll back.

changes: Item 1 (truncated-file refusal): HypothesisRegistry._load() now refuses when the parsed JSON is not an object, or when 'records' or the new 'family_manifests' key is missing or not a list. Previously a payload missing the 'records' key loaded silently as an empty registry.

Item 2 (family manifest sealing): new FamilyManifest dataclass (family_id, ordered member_ids, a manifest_hash sealing both, verified the same way PreRegistration's own seal is). register() creates or extends a family's manifest in registration order. Persisted as a top-level 'family_manifests' list; every load cross-checks each manifest's member set against the hypothesis records actually present, in both directions. A deleted hypothesis record, an added one spliced in outside register(), or an orphaned/mismatched manifest all now raise FamilyMembershipTamperedError - closing the path by which deleting a losing hypothesis could previously shrink the multiple-testing family and inflate the survivors' BH power undetected.

Item 3 (state hash chain): new StateTransition dataclass and a Merkle-style running fold hash (_fold_state_chain). Every HypothesisRecord carries state_chain (ordered transitions from a genesis None->REGISTERED link) and state_chain_hash. HypothesisRecord.initial() builds the genesis link at register(); .transitioned_to() extends and reseals the chain at every subsequent state change (advance(), the TEST-segment auto-transition in record_evaluation(), and adjudicate_family()'s promotion/rejection). verify_state_chain(), run on every load, checks fold-hash consistency, link continuity, that each transition beyond genesis is legal per research.lifecycle, and that the final link's to_state agrees with the stored state field - the concrete gap the brief named: a hand-edited state: CANDIDATE with no matching chain link now fails to load instead of loading as promoted.
hypothesis_registry_format_v3_hardening_.threat_model: Unchanged from the pre-existing preregistration_hash seal: tamper-evident via SHA-256 self-consistency, not tamper-proof against a sophisticated attacker with full file write access who could in principle forge an entire new internally-consistent structure. No HMAC or secret-key infrastructure exists in this codebase to do better, and introducing one was out of scope. Both new mechanisms therefore layer a second, independent check beyond hash self-consistency where one was cheaply available: the family manifest is cross-checked against the actual records (catches a self-consistent forged manifest), and the state chain is re-validated against research.lifecycle's legal transitions (catches a self-consistent forged chain).

findings.location: core/paper_trader.py:773-809 (_load_failed), called from the wrong-shape branch of load() at core/paper_trader.py:755-762
findings.summary: _load_failed() unconditionally passes exc_info=True to logger.error(). It is invoked from three places: two are inside an active except block (OSError -> UNREADABLE, ValueError/JSONDecodeError -> CORRUPT), where exc_info=True correctly attaches the real traceback; the third is the wrong-shape check after a successful json.load() (e.g. {"positions": [], "history": []}), which runs with no exception in flight. There, exc_info=True formats sys.exc_info() == (None, None, None), and Python's logging module appends a literal 'NoneType: None' line to the operator-facing ERROR record.
findings.evidence: Reproduced directly: logging.Logger.error(msg, exc_info=True) with no active exception appends 'NoneType: None' to the formatted record (verified with a throwaway StreamHandler in this session). The wrong-shape parametrized cases in tests/test_wrong_shape_is_corrupt_not_empty only assert load_status/positions/quarantine, not log content, so this was never exercised by an assertion.
findings.impact: Purely diagnostic: no effect on positions, load_status, quarantine behavior, halting, or any durable/financial state - PaperTrader is a passive, unread mirror regardless. The operator-visible defect is that an ERROR log line for this one specific corruption shape looks like it swallowed a real exception when none occurred, which could mislead incident triage reading Atlas logs.
findings.reasoning_for_low_not_higher: No financial, execution, or recovery-behavior consequence of any kind; confined to one log line's cosmetic content for one specific (already-rare) corruption shape.
findings.remediation: Pass exc_info only when an exception is actually in flight (e.g. exc_info=sys.exc_info()[0] is not None, or split _load_failed into two call shapes) rather than hard-coding True.
findings.status_reason: Task scope (per the authorizing instruction) was to fix BLOCKING/HIGH findings only; none were found. mechanism.hook_rationale: risk_check is the single place a RiskState is derived for RiskEngine evaluation, so the next request after the UTC date changes is covered whether the process restarted on a later day or ran uninterrupted through midnight. A startup-only check would miss the uninterrupted case; a MarketLoop per-cycle check would route financial-state mutation through the market path, which standing project doctrine forbids, and would add a second trigger to reconcile.
mechanism.mode_scope: PAPER only. Explicit branch: `if self.mode != self.MODE_PAPER: return` before any load, gate or write. LIVE (and any non-PAPER value) has no automatic path; the stale day stays fail-closed exactly as before.
safety_gate_all_required: transaction journal loaded and not load_failed (JOURNAL_NOT_LOADED)

F-2 orphan detection answerable (RESERVATION_STATE_UNVERIFIABLE) and empty (ORPHAN_RESERVATION_PRESENT) - detection extracted verbatim from _release_orphan_reservations into _orphan_reservation_ids(), shared by the startup sweep and this gate
durable equity finite and positive (abort before any write)
mechanism.gate_refusal_behavior: stored day untouched; WARNING logged with reason; RiskEngine then rejects with RISK_ACCOUNTING_DAY_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED exactly as before. One attempt per risk_check call; no internal retry loop.
mechanism.atomicity: gate, equity read, PREPARED audit write and durable save all run under ExecutionManager._lock AND ExecutionTransactionJournal._lock, so no journal prepare() can interleave between gate and write. Lock order manager->journal->leaf; independent audit found no reverse-order acquisition.
mechanism.rollover_semantics: unchanged JsonRiskStateStore.rollover: accounting_day_utc=today, realized_daily_pnl=0, peak_equity=max(previous peak, equity), current_equity=equity; atomic temp+fsync+os.replace; backwards day raises; same-day is a no-op
mechanism.audit: write-ahead RISK_ACCOUNTING_DAY_ROLLOVER_PREPARED (mandatory: failure aborts with no write) then RISK_ACCOUNTING_DAY_ROLLOVER_COMMITTED (causation_id=PREPARED event id). A COMMITTED write failure leaves the durable rollover in place, increments audit_write_failures and marks the audit runtime AUDIT_DEGRADED via _record_audit_failure. Successful rollover logged at WARNING.

migration_safety_checklist.idempotency: same-day call is a no-op (stored day >= today returns before gate); double fire and 8-thread concurrent fire tested: exactly one PREPARED/COMMITTED pair
migration_safety_checklist.resume: crash before os.replace leaves previous day byte-identical and no temp file; next request re-rolls from the unchanged previous state
migration_safety_checklist.retry: write failure leaves old day; next request retries once (no loop)
migration_safety_checklist.sequence_ordering: PREPARED audit -> durable save -> WARNING log -> COMMITTED audit
migration_safety_checklist.duplicates: crash after os.replace: restart sees today, no second rollover (tested: single PREPARED, no re-roll)
migration_safety_checklist.partial_state: impossible at file level (atomic replace); PREPARED without COMMITTED is the durable marker of an attempt that did not complete
migration_safety_checklist.conflicts: future stored day -> load raises -> RISK_STATE_RESTORATION_FAILED, never rolled backwards (tested)
migration_safety_checklist.rollback_recovery: no automatic rollback; a failed attempt leaves the previous durable day, which is the pre-change fail-closed state

defect_closed.summary: No production code updated JsonRiskStateStore.realized_daily_pnl, and current_equity/peak_equity were refreshed only at bootstrap and at the v4.81 day rollover, so RiskEngine's DAILY_LOSS_LIMIT_BREACHED check and drawdown ladder (DRAWDOWN_RESTRICT_NEW_RISK / DRAWDOWN_HALT_NEW_RISK) never evaluated real results.
defect_closed.reason_code_clarification: The authorizing prompt called the daily-loss limit DRAWDOWN_HALT_NEW_RISK. In core/risk_engine.py evaluate() these are distinct checks: realized daily loss >= ceiling rejects as DAILY_LOSS_LIMIT_BREACHED (evaluated first); peak-to-current drawdown >= drawdown_halt_pct rejects as DRAWDOWN_HALT_NEW_RISK. This change activates both. Neither sets execution_halted: both reject new-risk BUYs only; risk-reducing SELLs remain approvable.

mechanism.hook_in_point: ExecutionManager._finalize_durable_financial_state: pre-commit foundation.snapshot(), foundation.apply_confirmed(), and for a SELL whose apply was not replayed, _record_realized_risk_accounting(), all under ExecutionManager._lock + ExecutionTransactionJournal._lock (same order as the rollover: manager -> journal). Locks read defensively (getattr) so partially constructed test doubles finalize as before.
mechanism.scope_of_trigger: every non-replayed SELL apply - full exits and partial reductions (both realize P&L). BUY applies do not touch risk accounting.
mechanism.realized_pnl_definition: delta realized_gross_pnl - delta fees (exit fee) - released entry_fees (entry_fees before minus entry_fees remaining), all from ExecutionPortfolioFoundation snapshots either side of the commit, under SETTLEMENT_CONTEXT_PRECISION. Over a complete round trip this equals the change in the foundation's realized_net_pnl (tested).
mechanism.equity_source: current_equity = post-commit ExecutionPortfolioFoundation snapshot equity; peak_equity = max(stored peak, that equity). No independent equity computation.
mechanism.day_rule: stored accounting day must equal today; a mismatch (UTC midnight between admission and commit) is a recording failure, never booked to the prior day.
mechanism.audit: RISK_ACCOUNTING_REALIZED_PNL_PREPARED (write-ahead, mandatory when audit enabled) -> JsonRiskStateStore.save (existing atomic replace) -> RISK_ACCOUNTING_REALIZED_PNL_COMMITTED (causation_id = PREPARED). COMMITTED failure keeps the durable update and degrades audit, as the rollover.
mechanism.failure_behavior: Any recording failure raises RISK_ACCOUNTING_UPDATE_FAILED into execute()'s existing post-apply finalization-failure path: reservation marked INDETERMINATE, journal entry left COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN on disk, runtime halted (DURABLE_FINANCIAL_FINALIZATION_FAILED), result COMMIT_STATUS_UNKNOWN. Restart stays fail-closed on the unresolved journal.
mechanism.mode_scope: PAPER only: non-PAPER returns before any read or write. No LIVE path.
mechanism.store_changes: none - core/risk_state_store.py unchanged; RestoredRiskState and the existing save() reused.

fix.mechanism: New opt-in keyword sanitize_sensitive_data(..., preserve_identifiers=True), threaded through every recursion branch. Under it, a value held under an exact key in OPAQUE_IDENTIFIER_KEYS (request_id, execution_id, idempotency_key, execution_fingerprint, candle_identity, position_id, order_id, trade_id) is returned byte-exact when it is a non-empty string, not whitespace-padded, <= 200 characters, free of CR/LF/TAB/NUL and within the charset [A-Za-z0-9|:._-] (a UUID object serializes to its canonical string); a value under DIGEST_KEYS (instrument_rules_digest) only when it is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters. Anything else is redacted exactly as before. A sensitive key name still wins; the key sets are checked disjoint at import (explicit RuntimeError).
fix.opted_in_call_sites: ExecutionTransactionJournal (4), ExecutionIdempotencyStore._safe_payload, AuditEvent._safe_payload. No other caller changes behaviour.

venue_rules_refresh_low1_trailing_zero_c.finding: No code path was found that compares config/instrument_rules.json's decimal fields as raw text, or hashes the raw config bytes to detect a rules change. Every change-detection and idempotency-sealing path already goes through InstrumentRules.digest, whose _compute_digest calls Decimal.normalize() on quantity_step/min_quantity/min_notional/price_tick (and, when present, max_quantity/max_notional/market_max_quantity) before serializing to the canonical payload that is hashed. This normalization was already in place before this investigation (Block 5D M3 remediation) specifically to make the digest invariant to cosmetic trailing-zero representation, and is already covered by an existing regression test, tests/test_block5d_instrument_precision_contract.py::test_digest_ignores_cosmetic_trailing_zero_representation, which asserts digest parity between '0.00001'-style and '0.00001000'-style rules. The rederivation-refuses-when-instrument-rules-changed-since-admission behavior (tests/test_execution_crash_recovery_f1_f6.py::test_rederivation_refuses_when_instrument_rules_changed_since_admission, exercised via tools/reconcile_execution_authorities.py) is also digest-based and therefore already correctly treats a formatting-only republish as unchanged; it detects only a genuine economic value change (its test fixture uses a different quantity_step/min_notional/source/source_version, not a reformatted equal value).
venue_rules_refresh_low1_trailing_zero_c.no_fix_rationale: The safety property LOW-1 asked about - that trailing-zero-only formatting differences must never register as a rules 'change' - is already structurally enforced by the digest normalization added under Block 5D M3, and was already regression-tested before this session. Adding a new fix or a new test for an already-covered invariant would duplicate existing coverage without closing any real gap.

findings_FACT: The 'learning memory' (ai/core/atlas_memory_core.py via MemoryAdapter) does not learn from trades: nothing in the runtime calls record_trade/update_trade_outcome, and AtlasBrain passes memory_result to the decision builder as metadata only - it never changes confidence or action. This is deliberate (decision log #1): feeding it would raise confidence without evidence (rule 3, NB-4). The durable closed-position archive is the real performance record.

PAPER fills happen at the decision price = the last CLOSED 1-minute candle's close (up to ~60 s old; PERF-001 candle age p95 55.9 s) with the 0.1 %/side fee and NO slippage or spread: paper results are somewhat optimistic versus a real market order.
v5.33 backtest: every exit was a SELL signal and fees were 77 % of the plain EXP-001 loss - churn, not entries, is the dominant cost.
